candidate.title: Nextera™ Library Preparation
candidate.scope: The single Nextera DNA library-preparation outline in the assigned Illumina schematic: DNA association with transposase, tagmentation, the depicted index/P5/P7 end-assembly interface, and amplification to a product ready for cluster generation. The intermediate end-assembly drawing is an interface, without an asserted internal annealing or fill-in sequence. No kit version, biological origin of the DNA, or alternative workflow is specified; cluster generation and sequencing are downstream of the depicted endpoint.

states.label: DNA input
features: Continuous parallel blue lines labelled DNA, supporting a double-stranded input representation.
The source identifies the substrate as DNA without identifying a specimen, genomic locus, or upstream preparation.

evidence.locator: Top horizontal double blue line labelled DNA.

states.label: Transposase reagent with colored arms
features: Two blue icons labelled Transposase, one with magenta arms and one with green arms.
These are reagent/catalyst depictions, not independent workflow branches; the drawing does not specify the enzyme identity or arm sequences.

evidence.locator: Top region: two blue Transposase icons bearing magenta and green arms.

states.label: DNA associated with transposase
features: Blue transposase icons sit at two positions on the still-continuous double-line DNA.
Magenta and green arms remain at the respective transposase/DNA interfaces.

evidence.locator: Second DNA drawing: blue transposase icons positioned on the DNA, retaining magenta and green arms.

states.label: Tagmented DNA fragments
features: Discontinuous double-line blue DNA with short magenta and green terminal segments.
A representative central DNA segment is annotated ~300bp; this does not specify a uniform fragment size.
Short blue pieces remain visible outside the two colored junctions; the next drawing follows a representative insert with magenta and green ends, without an explicit branching or selection operation.

evidence.locator: Middle region: downward arrow from enzyme-associated DNA, Tagmentation label, discontinuous double-line DNA with magenta/green segments and ~300bp annotation.

states.label: Tagged DNA with index/P5/P7-bearing end extensions
features: Central double-line blue insert retains magenta left and green right terminal regions.
Outward left extension is labelled P5 and Index 2; outward right extension is labelled Index 1 and P7.
This is the drawn end-assembly interface; a precise strand-fill or primer-extension history is not assigned.

evidence.locator: Arrow below tagged fragments to the double-line insert with outward arms labelled P5 and Index 2 on the left, Index 1 and P7 on the right.

states.label: Product ready for cluster generation
features: Final sequence layout has P5 at the left, Index 2 inward of P5, a central blue DNA-derived insert, Index 1 toward the right, and P7 at the right.
Both labelled index regions and the terminal P5/P7 regions occur in the same library layout as the insert.
The final single-line icon describes the library layout without establishing a strand-specific product state.

evidence.locator: Bottom product drawing: P5, Index 2, blue insert, Index 1, P7 and Product ready for cluster generation.

operations.label: Transposase–DNA association (unlabelled first arrow)
operations.description: The first arrow connects separate DNA and transposase reagent depictions to a DNA-associated transposase state. The blue DNA remains continuous at this boundary. Transposase is a reagent/catalyst input; the drawing does not establish its consumption.
operations.information_effect: Associates the differently colored transposase arms with positions on the input DNA; no biological identifier is labelled at this stage.

evidence.locator: Upper region: Transposase icons with magenta/green arms, double-line DNA, and first downward arrow to enzyme-associated DNA.

operations.label: Tagmentation
operations.description: The transposase-associated continuous DNA becomes a set of shorter DNA pieces with magenta/green terminal regions. A representative central segment is labelled ~300bp.
operations.mechanism: Transposase-associated DNA fragmentation and terminal tagging at the level shown; detailed end chemistry is unspecified.
operations.information_effect: The internal blue segments retain portions of the input DNA while the colored terminal regions provide the depicted interface to the subsequent library-end assembly.

evidence.locator: Middle region: downward arrow from enzyme-associated DNA, Tagmentation label, discontinuous double-line DNA with magenta/green segments and ~300bp annotation.

evidence.rationale: The change from continuous blue DNA with enzyme-associated colored arms to blue fragments with matching colored ends supports coupled fragmentation and tagging. No enzyme species, exact sequence, or end-group chemistry is inferred.

operations.label: Index/P5/P7 end-assembly interface (unlabelled arrow)
operations.description: The arrow below the tagmented fragments leads to a representative tagged insert with outward end extensions labelled P5/Index 2 on the left and Index 1/P7 on the right. This records the appearance of those components without assigning a separate unshown biochemical sequence to their assembly.
operations.information_effect: Positions the two labelled index regions and P5/P7 regions at opposite ends of the DNA-derived insert. Index-to-sample or index-to-cell assignments are not supplied.

evidence.locator: Arrow below tagged fragments to the double-line insert with outward arms labelled P5 and Index 2 on the left, Index 1 and P7 on the right.

operations.label: Amplification
operations.description: The tailed DNA intermediate is amplified to the final library layout bearing P5, Index 2, the DNA-derived insert, Index 1 and P7. The resulting product is explicitly labelled ready for cluster generation.
operations.information_effect: The readout carrier is the DNA insert physically linked to both labelled index regions and P5/P7 ends. Interpreting the persistent blue insert as input-derived sequence, subsequent sequencing could recover sequence from portions of the input DNA. The schematic supplies no narrower biological-target association or sequencing data.

evidence.locator: Lower region: downward arrow from the tailed intermediate, Amplification label, and final P5–Index 2–insert–Index 1–P7 sequence layout beside Product ready for cluster generation.

evidence.rationale: The same blue internal material is traced from input DNA through fragments to the final insert; this supports representation of input-DNA subsequences, while no sample origin or upstream RNA-to-DNA conversion is depicted.
